raw:
Thessaly folds the sweet wrapper into a narrow strip.

“Then the obligation ended when the work ended. Fine. A finished contract can still be useful, though. It tells you who thought an unnamed library was worth paying for.”

“Keep it,” Aldric says. “If only so Academy counsel can confirm that the terms ended as you understand them.”

Ashara reaches for another piece of bread. “Enough paperwork. He’s trying to eat.”

Caelindra samples a glazed root vegetable and makes a faint face. “The kitchen appears to have mistaken sweetness for seasoning.”

Ysolde considers her own forkful. “It is sweet.”

“That is not a defense.”

“It was not intended as one.”

Ashara’s laugh catches Rashid’s, brief and unwilling. Then she turns to him.

“Octagon after dinner. Half an hour.”

“Yes,” Rashid says. “I remember.”

“Useful faculty.”

“Rarely appreciated.”

From the common room comes the crisp snap of cards being shuffled. A moment later, a young demon woman appears in the dining-hall arch with her splinted wrist tucked close to her side. Two other students linger behind her near the firelit doorway.

Her eyes settle on Rashid.

“Cards are out,” she says. “You said you’d be there right after dinner.”
